::: {.lead}
Today you check information before you use it, and you share and use
things safely: a claim from a message, a picture for a report, an app on
your phone, and an AI prompt. Each experiment has two parts. **Part A** is
in a browser, Word or an AI assistant on the computer. **Part B** is on
your phone or on a simulator of the interactive lesson: on paper, scan its
QR code; on the screen, click its link. After each step, write your result
in its box: a name, a number, a word, or yes or no.
:::

## Before you start

- **You need:** a computer with a browser, a search engine (`bing.com`),
  Word, an AI assistant that the university allows (for example
  `copilot.microsoft.com`), and your phone.
- **No lab computer today?** Your teacher does Part A on the screen, on the
  simulators of the interactive lesson and in an AI assistant. Do Part B on
  your phone.
- **Never type personal data** into an AI tool: this lecture shows how to
  keep it out.
- **Check:** the results are at the end of this worksheet. Look only after
  you try. On the interactive lesson, every step has a check that answers
  at once.

## Experiment 1 · Check a claim in two sources

**The idea:** a **claim** is a sentence that can be checked: a number, a
date, a name, a fact. A claim can come from a message, a website or an AI
answer. Check it outside the place where you read it, in two **reliable
sources** that agree, for example an encyclopedia and an official website.
A source that nobody can find is not a source: delete the claim.

**Aim:** check a claim in two reliable sources.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (a search engine)**
:::

1. A message in your class group says: "The highest mountain in Jordan is
   Jabal Ram, 1 734 m." Search for **highest mountain in Jordan** and
   check it in **two reliable sources**.

   {{< record "The highest mountain … ; its height …" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Two reliable sources give **Jabal Umm al-Dami** (جبل أم الدامي), about
   **1 850 m**, in the south near Wadi Rum. Jabal Ram is lower: the message
   is wrong.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A message says: "The highest mountain in Jordan is Jabal Ram, 1 734 m." Two
   reliable sources say Jabal Umm al-Dami, about 1 850 m. What do you write?

   - [x] Jabal Umm al-Dami, about 1 850 m

     Why: Two reliable sources that agree show a true claim: correct the message with the sources.

   - [ ] Jabal Ram, 1 734 m

     Why: One message is not a source.

   - [ ] Nothing: the message and the sources disagree.

     Why: Two reliable sources that agree are enough to correct the message.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/fact-check-lab.html" poster="sims/fact-check-lab.png" title="Fact-Check Lab: Sami's AI draft" >}}

2. In **Fact-Check Lab**, decide for each claim of Sami's text: keep,
   correct or remove. How many do you remove?

   {{< record "Claims to remove" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **2** to remove. **Keep:** 7 hours of sleep, and a short nap of 20 minutes.
   **Correct:** the brain uses about 20 % (not 50 %), and the library opens
   at 8:00 (not 7:00). **Remove:** Miller & Hart (2019) and the Einstein
   quote: nothing reliable shows them.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Keep, correct or remove? Sort the six claims of Sami's text.

   Keep
   :   We need about 7 hours of sleep.

       Why: Reliable sources agree.

   :   A short nap lasts 20 minutes.

       Why: Reliable sources agree.

   Correct
   :   The brain uses 50 % of the body's energy.

       Why: Sources say about 20 %.

   :   The library opens at 7:00.

       Why: The library page says 8:00.

   Remove
   :   A study by Miller & Hart (2019)

       Why: Nothing reliable shows this study: a made-up source.

   :   The quote of Einstein

       Why: Nothing reliable shows that he said it.
   :::

## Experiment 2 · Share and use safely

**The idea:** what you share and use online has rules. **Personal data**
(an ID number, a phone number, an address, the grades or the photo of
another person) is not shared without permission. A picture from a
website is protected by **copyright**: use a free picture (Word's **Stock
Images**, your own photo) or ask, and say where it comes from with a
**source line**. On the phone, an app gets only the **permissions** that
its job needs.

**Aim:** use a free picture with its source, and give an app only what it
needs.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (Word)**
:::

1. In Word, choose **Insert › Pictures › Stock Images**, search
   **library**, and insert a picture. Can you use it in a report? (yes /
   no)

   {{< record "I can use it (yes / no)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Yes.** The stock images of Office are free to use in your documents.
   A picture from an image search is not free: it belongs to its owner.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which picture can you put in your class report without asking anyone?

   - [x] a stock image of Word (Insert › Pictures › Stock Images)

     Why: The stock images of Office are free to use in your documents.

   - [ ] any picture from an image search

     Why: A picture on a website belongs to its owner: ask, or use a free one.

   - [ ] a classmate's photo from the class group

     Why: A photo of a person is personal data: ask first.
   :::

2. Under a photo of Petra from the website *Visit Jordan*, type: **Picture:
   Visit Jordan, visitjordan.com, 10 Nov 2026**.

   {{< record "The three parts of my source line" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **Who** (Visit Jordan), **where** (visitjordan.com) and **when** (the
   date you took it). "Google" or "the Internet" is not a source.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which source line is right under the photo of Petra?

   - [x] Picture: Visit Jordan, visitjordan.com, 10 Nov 2026

     Why: It names who, where and when, so the reader can find the picture.

   - [ ] Picture: Google

     Why: Google finds pictures; it does not own them.

   - [ ] Picture: the Internet

     Why: The Internet is not a source: the reader cannot find the picture.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On your phone**
:::

3. On your phone, open **Settings › Apps** (iPhone: **Settings ›
   Privacy**) and the **Permissions** of one app. Does it use your
   location?

   {{< record "The app … ; location (yes / no)" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   Each phone is different. A map app needs your location; a calculator or
   a flashlight does not. Switch off a permission that the app's job does
   not need.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   A new flashlight app asks for your contacts and your location. What do you do?

   - [x] Deny both: a flashlight needs neither.

     Why: An app gets only the permissions that its job needs.

   - [ ] Allow both: apps always need them.

     Why: A flashlight needs only the light of the camera.

   - [ ] Allow the contacts only.

     Why: A flashlight has nothing to do with your contacts.
   :::

## Experiment 3 · AI: a safe prompt and an honest statement

**The idea:** never type personal data into an AI tool: names, phone
numbers, addresses, ID numbers or grades of real people. Write a
**placeholder** instead, for example [name] or [phone], and add the real
details later, outside the AI. When you use AI for your work, say so: an
**AI-use statement** names the tool, says what the AI did, what you changed
and how you checked it.

**Aim:** clean a prompt, and say honestly how you used AI.

::: {.part}
**Part A · In the app (an AI assistant and Word)**
:::

1. Your neighbour's water tank leaks. Copy this **clean** prompt into the
   AI assistant: its personal data has placeholders. Which ones?

   ::: {.prompt}
   Write a short message to [neighbour], phone [phone], of [address]: the
   water tank on our roof leaks, and a plumber comes on Tuesday at 10:00.
   :::

   {{< record "The placeholders in the clean prompt" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **[neighbour]**, **[phone]** and **[address]**: personal data stays out of
   the AI. The leak, Tuesday and 10:00 stay: the AI needs them. You add the
   real name later, outside the AI.
   :::

   ::: {.choice}
   Which prompt is clean?

   - [x] Write a short message to [neighbour], phone [phone], of [address]: the water tank on our roof leaks, and a plumber comes on Tuesday at 10:00.

     Why: The personal data has placeholders; the leak, Tuesday and 10:00 stay.

   - [ ] Write a short message to Khaled Nasser, phone 0790000000, of 5 Olive Street: the water tank on our roof leaks …

     Why: The name, the phone and the address are personal data.

   - [ ] Write a short message to [neighbour]: [problem] on [day] at [time].

     Why: The AI needs the leak, the day and the time; they say nothing about who the person is.
   :::

2. Paste the AI message into Word and type under it, with your tool and
   date: **I used Microsoft Copilot on 15 December 2026 to draft this
   message. I added the names and checked the day and time.**

   {{< record "The tool and the date in my statement" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   The tool (Microsoft Copilot, or the one that you used) and the date. A
   complete statement names the tool, says what the AI did, what you
   changed and how you checked it. The part that students forget most is
   **the check**.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   Which part of the statement is each sentence? Sort them.

   The tool
   :   I used Microsoft Copilot.

       Why: It names the AI tool.

   What the AI did
   :   It drafted the message to my neighbour.

       Why: It says what the AI made.

   What you changed
   :   I added the names myself.

       Why: It says what is yours.

   How you checked
   :   I checked the day and the time.

       Why: It says how you checked the AI's work.
   :::

::: {.part}
**Part B · On the simulator** (no computer? do it on your phone)
:::

{{< sim file="sims/prompt-cleaner.html" poster="sims/prompt-cleaner.png" title="Prompt Cleaner: no personal data in the chat" >}}

3. In **Prompt Cleaner**, clean **Huda's reminder**. How many parts get a
   placeholder?

   {{< record "Placeholders" >}}

   ::: {.check}
   **3**. The name becomes **[Customer]**, the e-mail **[e-mail]** and the bank
   account **[bank account]**. **340 JD** and **March** stay: the AI needs
   them, and they say nothing about who the person is.
   :::

   ::: {.sort}
   A placeholder, or keep it? Sort the parts of Huda's reminder.

   Replace with a placeholder
   :   the name of the customer

       Why: A name shows who the person is.

   :   the bank account

       Why: Bank details are private.

   Keep: the AI needs it
   :   340 JD

       Why: The amount says nothing about who the person is.

   :   March

       Why: The month is needed for the reminder.
   :::
